results.title: Dambazau, Business Leaders Put Payments, Export Finance, Investment At Centre of CBN Roundtable.
results.description:
Dambazau, Business Leaders Put Payments, Export Finance, Investment At Centre of CBN Roundtable. 

Nigeria’s Ambassador to China, Lt Gen Abdulrahman Bello Dambazau (rtd), has outlined practical  financial priorities for deeper bilateral ties, including reliable cross-border payments, export  finance and long-term  investment.

Speaking at the Central Bank of Nigeria’s ‘Strengthening the Nigeria–China Financial Corridor’ roundtable in Beijing, Dambazau said financial cooperation should deliver measurable benefits for businesses and citizens in both countries.
“For businesses, financial cooperation has a practical meaning. It means paying a supplier reliably, receiving export earnings promptly, securing affordable working capital, and obtaining long-term finance for a viable investment,” he said.

“Our task is to make these transactions easier, more transparent and more accessible.”
The Ambassador’s contribution opened a discussion in which Nigerian and Chinese businesses connected the financial corridor’s wider ambitions with their experience of settlement, investment and access to financial services.

Dambazau emphasised the importance of clear information on payment channels, transaction costs and settlement times. Stronger commercial-bank relationships, supported by effective engagement between regulators, could help resolve operational difficulties and reduce uncertainty, he said.

“Payment delay can become a shipment delay, a production interruption or a lost business opportunity,” he said.

On local-currency settlement, he said the bilateral swap framework’s value to businesses depended on access, adequate liquidity, competitive pricing and a clear understanding of how the arrangements worked. Settlement in local currencies should remain a commercial choice supported by transparent terms and sound risk management.

He also called for financial cooperation that supported Nigerian production and exports.

“Export finance, letters of credit, credit insurance, and working capital facilities can help businesses turn market opportunities into completed transactions,” he said.

Dambazau advocated stronger financial flows in both directions, connecting finance with the practical requirements of supplying the Chinese market. 

He also highlighted patient capital for productive investment and safeguards that protected legitimate commerce while allowing smaller businesses to participate.

The embassy, he said, stood ready to facilitate connections and bring commercial concerns to the appropriate institutions.

CIG Motors Chairman Diana Chen reinforced the importance of predictability from the perspective of a Chinese business with an established operating presence in Nigeria.

She described the company’s factories and employment of Nigerian engineers, technicians and managers as evidence of a relationship extending beyond imports into production and skills development.

“What we ask for today is not grand architecture. It is continuity, predictability, and the right confidence that when we commit capital, we will one day be able to bring our returns home in good order,” she said.

Chen said the financial system should keep pace with Chinese businesses’ evolution in Nigeria, including their need for patient capital alongside short-term trade finance.

Nigerian businessman, Festus Mbisiogu, welcomed the opportunity for operators in China to explain payment difficulties directly to the CBN leadership. 

He described uncertainty over settlement routes, suppliers requesting RMB payments and transactions delayed within banking channels.

Flutterwave CEO, Olugbenga Agboola, credited improvements in Nigeria’s compliance infrastructure and international credibility with strengthening the environment in which Nigerian financial businesses engaged foreign counterparts. 

He commended CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso and his team for implementing their policy direction.

results.title: China backs Tinubu's economic reforms and seeks continuity beyond 2027.👍 China's Ambassador to Nigeria, Yu Dunhai, has expressed confidence
results.description:
China backs Tinubu's economic reforms and seeks continuity beyond 2027.👍
China's Ambassador to Nigeria, Yu Dunhai, has expressed confidence in Nigeria's economic reforms and called for their consolidation beyond 2027.

Nigeria–China bilateral trade reached $18 billion in the first half of 2026.👌

results.title: Let it be on the record: Buhari birthed this project from start to finish.
results.description:
Let it be on the record: Buhari birthed this project from start to finish.

Groundbreaking & physical work started in 2021.

Buhari kept it alive with $318M in direct FG cash when the lender, China EXIM Bank, stalled and backed out due to post-COVID adjustments. 

Before leaving office in May 2023, Buhari restructured the financing to secure the €245M from China Development Bank loan with the 9th Senate. 

Tinubu can't claim this project.

results.title: The Orange Group and @KPMG Nigeria, did an interesting study on Smartphone Penetration in Nigeria.
results.description:
The Orange Group and @KPMG Nigeria, did an interesting study on Smartphone Penetration in Nigeria.

Chinese brands dominate; with one company (Transsion - Itel, Infinix, Tecno) - accounting for almost 60% of smartphones.
Link to study is here: https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/ng/pdf/2026/09/Nigeria%20Smartphone%20Study%20-%20Orange%20Group%20and%20KPMG.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf
